speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a concerning rash and recent health changes; to begin our assessment, have you experienced any fever, night sweats, or significant weight loss lately? Also, have you noticed any joint pain or fatigue accompanying your skin symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful context; given the arthritis management and new cough, could you describe the appearance and distribution of the rash in detail, and has it appeared on your face or mucous membranes? Also, have you noticed any shortness of breath or chest pain?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, ANA, Rheumatoid Factor.
REQUEST IMAGES: [Full body dermatology photo, Chest X-Ray].

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with mucocutaneous involvement. The combination of a new rash, arthritis, cough, and mucositis in a 47-year-old male is highly suggestive of this systemic autoimmune disease, which requires immediate confirmation via the requested labs and imaging.
